s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic papular skin lesions with pruritus and follicular involvement
salient_findings: Numerous whitish papules on the back of more than 10 years' duration
Papules became pruritic and extended to the waist and anterior trunk
Folliculocentric papules with central keratin plugs and surrounding erythema
key_facts: Woman in her 60s presented with skin lesions
Lesions previously resolved with topical corticosteroids but flared after treatment discontinuation
No family history of similar lesions
Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area
Most lesions were folliculocentric under close inspection
Dermoscopy revealed central keratin plugs and structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas
Antinuclear antibody and hyperglobulinemia tests were negative
Biopsy specimen showed central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy
Papillary dermis was markedly thickened with homogenized collagens and sparse bandlike lymphocytic infiltration
Some eosinophils in infiltrate and red blood cell extravasation
Congo red and mucicarmine stains were negative for amyloid and mucin

shortlist.label: Keratosis Pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Folliculocentric papules and central keratin plugs on dermoscopy

shortlist.label: Lichen Spinulosus
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules with follicular involvement

shortlist.label: Keratosis Follicularis
shortlist.why_kept: Follicular plugs and epidermal atrophy on histopathology

shortlist.label: Follicular Lichenoid Dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Sparse bandlike lymphocytic infiltration and eosinophils on histopathology

shortlist.label: Darier Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Keratotic papules and follicular involvement with negative family history

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules that are folliculocentric, along with dermoscopic findings of central keratin plugs and structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas, supports the diagnosis of Lichen Spinulosus. The histopathologic examination showing central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy also aligns with this condition.

rejected.label: Keratosis Pilaris
rejected.why: While Keratosis Pilaris involves folliculocentric lesions, it typically presents with rough, dry skin and does not fully match the described histopathologic and dermoscopic findings.

rejected.label: Keratosis Follicularis
rejected.why: This condition is less likely as it does not fully align with the combination of clinical, dermoscopic, and histopathologic findings presented in the case.

rejected.label: Follicular Lichenoid Dermatitis
rejected.why: The specific combination of clinical and histopathologic findings, including the presence of central keratin plugs and the pattern of inflammation, does not perfectly match Follicular Lichenoid Dermatitis.

rejected.label: Darier Disease
rejected.why: Darier Disease typically involves greasy, crusted papules in seborrheic areas and characteristic suprabasal acantholysis on histology, which does not match the provided case details.
